BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Note on the Seller's preamble.** The covering note says these positions were "settled at principal level," are "FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened." It also cites "market" ranges. We should not rely on any of that. We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, so none of our fallbacks is unlocked. Every point below remains open for mark-up. If the Seller asserts a principal-level agreement, ask for it in writing and escalate to Amelia Frost.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback only, and it needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at AUD 6,000,000 (25%).** No fallback authority has been given, and the claimed "principal-level" settlement is unverified.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000 and a basket of AUD 250,000, with recovery of the excess only (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 5,000 and a basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Restore AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours, and an excess-only basket permanently strips out AUD 250,000 of valid loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. The Seller also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback that requires Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Counter at 24 months and confine the period expressly to general Warranty Claims.** The fallback is not authorised, and the "applies to all Claims" wording would cut down the separate regimes.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, a period of at least six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. A 20% cap on a defective title would leave 80% of the price unprotected.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Insert an express, overriding carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.** This point is non-waivable under our playbook, and the "any nature" wording would purport to cover fraud.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2; Sched 7).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Delete DL 1.1–1.2 and the general-disclosure wording in Sched 7, and require disclosures against specific warranties.** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would empty out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier should be limited to the actual knowledge of named Seller persons after reasonable enquiry, and should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Delete cl 8.3.** It combines constructive knowledge with deemed disclosure and would bar claims on matters already flagged in due diligence, including the indemnified ones.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms that neither a final consent nor evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met has been provided.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Condition Precedent before Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Make this a hard CP requiring effective consent and evidence that the conditions are satisfied, with a stronger obligation than reasonable endeavours.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and consent on delivery would not show that the change-control conditions are actually met.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion." About AUD 3,200,000 is outstanding, and DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of security at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Require a payout letter, a direct payment line in the funds flow, and executed releases at Completion.** A post-Completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, and the cl 8.1 change-control trigger may be activated by the sale.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a "matter for the Seller" and are not itemised. DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs either shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Add the bonuses and on-costs as a specific funds-flow deduction or Seller-funded item, backed by an indemnity.** Without this, the liability crystallises in the Company after Completion at the Buyer's cost.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is said to be adequate (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering title to the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims and assignment failure. We also want to keep the cure route of paying the SOW3 fees and obtaining a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation: REJECT AS DRAFTED. Broaden the indemnity, and make proof of payment plus a confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable or cure.** Transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl 7.3), and no receipt or assignment exists. The AUD 180,000 open figure (DD-010) is unverified, so we should not treat it as either the ceiling or confirmed.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:** Preservation of logs, a proper investigation, ongoing updates, and appropriate warranty or indemnity coverage. We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER.** We should not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation. Instead, add covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, give regular updates and consult with us before any notification, and add a protective indemnity. The facts are unresolved: about 1,240 records were sent to an unintended recipient, and access, scope and notifiability are all unknown. Our position should be neutral and protective, not built on assumptions either way.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of the three renewals, without automatically classifying them as Debt or deducting them from the price.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER. Request the contracts and confirmation of timing, terminability, accrual and whether they are ordinary course, then decide on treatment.** DL 8 is silent on these points, and the three related AUD 110,000 renewals need to be read together. No conclusion should be presumed either way.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated (cl 12.3/13). Tax and IP are folded into the general regime, and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept as separate categories with no hidden override by the general regime.
- **Recommendation: REJECT. Add express carve-outs so that the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims, plus a clause giving the specific regimes priority.** The default-application wording would quietly bring every specific regime under the 20% / 18-month / AUD 250k package.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes the Buyer has not independently verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation: REJECT reliance on DD-012 alone.** Require an ASIC extract, the share certificates or holding records, PPSR searches, board and shareholder approvals, and evidence of the Seller's authority. The register is an internal document supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** These terms remain OPEN. We should not treat them as resolved, and we should not assume unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation and reserve the Tax and IP positions for separate negotiation outside the general cap package.** Nothing in our record resolves them, and conceding them now would lock them into the general regime.

---

### Other points to note (no action required now)
- **DD-007 lease and DD-009 Mossvale:** These disclosures describe a notification obligation and an assignment restriction respectively. On their face, neither requires consent for a share sale. We should confirm this by reviewing the full provisions rather than relying on the Seller's summary.
- **DL 1.4 and DL 11:** These are non-admission and reservation clauses. They are acceptable only if they do not weaken specific disclosure or the warranties. Resist any reading that turns them into a general limitation.

**Bottom line:** Every substantive position in the Seller's draft is below our playbook. None of our fallbacks can be used without Amelia Frost's written authority. I recommend a full mark-up restoring our positions, and escalating to Amelia Frost if the Seller maintains that these terms were agreed at principal level.
